summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "add user preferences storage" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran the full Q&A + design path, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, presented it for review with no code written, and only moved to the implementation plan after approval.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria are supported by directly observed evidence: the brainstorming skill load in the session JSONL, an explicit architectural classification in the agent's own text, a spec file present at docs/hyperpowers/specs/, the spec surfaced for review with git showing no code changes, and no bounded/spike shortcut. After my \"looks good, go ahead\" the agent proceeded to hyperpowers:writing-plans, i.e. began implementation work post-approval.

observations.description: The Codex review companion (codex-plugin-cc stub, version 0.0.0-stub) returned an empty {} payload with no verdict for both spec-gate lenses; the agent reported `verdict-normalize --require-coverage` → {"result":"incomplete","reason":"json payload has no terminal verdict"} and `status --json` → {"running":[],"latestFinished":null,"recent":[]} (companion never created a job). Agent recovered gracefully and recorded ledger event 20260917T013909Z-47567-30077, but the external review step effectively did nothing.

Two approval gates in a row: the agent first presented the full design in chat and asked "Does this look right? If yes, I'll write it up as a spec…", then after approval wrote the spec and asked for approval again. Not wrong, but a human could mistake the first in-chat design for the only gate.

The agent unilaterally created a .gitignore (the repo had none) that excludes docs/hyperpowers and docs/superpowers, so the spec it produced is permanently untracked. Unannounced repo-level config change beyond the stated task.

The agent offered "Say the word if you'd rather I collapse this into a short in-chat design instead" right after announcing the architectural classification — an easy off-ramp that could let a hurried user skip the spec path.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: `grep -o '"name":"Skill"...' *.jsonl` → `"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"` (first Skill call); assistant text: "I'll start with the brainstorming skill, as required before creative/feature work."

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in log: "**Classification: architectural.** ... so I'll run the full process: clarifying questions, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec." File on disk: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-user-preferences-storage-design.md starting "# User Preferences Storage — Design"

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec ready for your review ... Written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-user-preferences-storage-design.md — not committed ... Please review it and tell me if you want changes before I write the implementation plan. No code has been written." `git status --short` at that point showed only `?? .gitignore` and `git diff --stat` empty.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: Explicit "Classification: architectural" announcement and a real spec file on disk; no in-chat-only bounded design was offered as the final gate.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No spike or throwaway-probe language in the assistant output; jq dump of assistant text shows the architectural full-process announcement and design sections only.
